full_judgment:
3. The petitioner's case in Writ Petition No. 207/86 is that they purchased the land in question from one Siddique Ahmed by a registered kabala dated 15.8.79. Originally the land was recorded in the name of its owner Abdur Rahman in RS khatian. Subsequently Fazar Rahman, the heir of Abdur Rahman, sold the same to one Nur Mohammad by registered deed of sale and Nur Mohammad sold the same in favour of one Siddique Ahmed by a registered kabala dated 3.12.69. The present petitioners purchased the suit land from the said Siddique Ahmed. The petitioners claim that the suit land be recorded in their names. That one Mohammad Harunur Rashid filed an objection under section 19(1) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in objection Case No. 139 dated 15.10.1980 objecting the entry of the name of the respondent No.2 in the draft record of rights. The objection was not allowed. 

 9. Mr. SC Das, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents submitted that the Director of Land Records has been vested with full powers and authority to revise any order passed by any Revenue Officer under Rule 44 read with Rule 43 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules, 1955 and as such committed no error of law. 

 11. Under section 19 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the Revenue Officer shall publish a draft of the record-of-rights so prepared or revised in the prescribed manner and shall receive and consider any objections relating to any entry therein during the period of such publication. By sub-section 2 of section 19 the forum for appeal is created and any aggrieved person by the order of the Revenue-Officer on any objection made under sub-section (1) of section 19 may appeal to the prescribed Revenue Authority not below the rank of an Assistant Settlement Officer in the manner and within such period as prescribed. 

 13. It appears that the respondent No.2 filed a Review petition before the appellate authority who by his order dated 27.3.85 rejected the same and maintained the earlier order dated 16.9.84 passed in the appeal. Thereafter the respondent No. 2 moved the Director General of Land Records respondent No. 1 in a second Review. The Director General of Land Records by the impugned order dated 31.3.86 allowed the second review petition by setting aside the order dated 16.9.84 of the appellate authority directing fresh hearing by one Mr. Bazlur Rahman, an Appeal officer. The Director General appears to have exercised his powers under Rule 44 of the East Bengal Tenancy Rules 1955 and caused interference under Rule 42 of the said Rules by holding that he had powers to correct, modify or set aside any record of rights made or passed in any proceeding following Rule Nos. 28-32 of the said rules. 

 14. Let us have a look at Rule 44 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955 which reads as follows: 

 15. Chapter XVII of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 deals with maintenance of the Record-of-Rights. Section 143 of the said Act runs as follows: 

 (d) the abatement of rent on account of abandonment or diluvian or acquisition of land." 

 16. Rule 36 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1951 speaks of Grant and Revision of certificate under section 20(4) which reads as follows: 

 Rule 38 speaks about Revision of record- of-rights under section 31 and Rule 39 deals with powers vested in Settlement and Assistant Settlement Officers and 40 deals with further power vested in Assistant Settlement Officer under Bengal Act V of 1875 and rule 41 empowers the Revenue Officer appointed with the additional designation of 'Settlement Officer' is also hereby vested with all the powers of superintendence of Survey under the Bengal Survey Act of 1875; Rule 42 of the Tenancy Rules reads as follows: 

 "A Revenue Officer appointed with the additional designation of 'Settlement Officer' may at any time before the publication of final record-of-rights, direct that any portion of the proceedings referred to in rules 28-32 in respect of any district, part of district or local area shall be cancelled and that the proceedings shall be taken up fresh from such stage as he may direct" From the aforesaid Rules it appears that the Director General of Land Records is vested with administrative control in respect of all operation under Chapter XVII of the Act and he may discharge all the functions of a Revenue Officer and shall have powers of a Settlement Officer under Rules 36, 38, 39, 42B as such the Director General of Land Records can be said to have at best co-equal powers with that of any Revenue Officer or Settlement Officer with regard to their powers whether they are designated as Additional Designation of Settlement Officer or not but this does not mean that the Director of Land Records has been vested with superior powers to sit over their orders or decisions and to annul the same. In a quasi judicial proceedings like the present one all that is competent to do is that he may exercise any of such powers as is vested in a Revenue or Settlement Officer under Rules 44 and 42 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955 in respect of a proceeding which has not attained finality, in either words, in a fresh proceeding the Director General is quite competent to assume his jurisdiction and dispose of the matter which is co-extensive with that of the Revenue or Settlement Officer. But in a matter which has already been disposed of by the Revenue Officer, namely Settlement Officer or Assistant Settlement Officer, in our view the Director of Land Records is incompetent and absolutely without power to lay his hands over such matters. 

 17. In the present cases the Director General of Land Records has interfered with the decisions of the appellate Court which has been done under sub-section 2 of section 19. But in administrative matter under chapter 17 of the Act he has been placed in superior position in matters of control, management of Record of Rights as vested under Rule 44 of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Rules. 

 The Respondent No. 1 Director General of Land Records Bangladesh has exceeded his power in entertaining and disposing of the second review petitions reviewing the orders passed by the Settlement Officer in appellate jurisdiction and as such his actions cannot but be said to be without jurisdiction. The Rule 19(1) and 19(2) has vested a power to the Settlement Officer to entertain and hear an appeal arising out of any disputed proceeding and no further power has been provided by way of revision. Although the Code of Civil Procedure has allowed an appellate authority to review any decision but no second review is contemplated under the Rule ref. by any third party namely, the Director of Land Records. Sub-section 3 of section 19 has clearly stated that when all such objections and appeals have been considered and disposed of according to such Rules, the Revenue-Officer shall finally frame the record and shall cause record to be finally published in the prescribed manner and the publication shall be conclusive evidence that the record has been duly prepared or revised under this Chapter. So after the forum of appeal being exhausted, the only course left open to the Revenue Officer is to finally frame the record and such record be published in the prescribed manner. So this Rule also does not speak of any forum created for hearing a second review petition as the respondent No. 1 has entertained and disposed of. Since the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act of 1950 and the Rules made thereunder do not specifically confer on the Director of Land Records any power to revise the order passed in appeal, in our view, the impugned orders dated 31.3.86 Annexure E in Writ Petition No. 207 and 'G' in Writ Petition No. 208 of 1986 are illegal and void and as such are hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and the same are of no legal effect.
